LayoutEditor__Description: Layout Editor (port Phase 5): sheets of drawings. A sheet is a paper size with a title block, free-placed viewports onto the project's plans, elevations, sections and 3D scenes at locked scales, and its own text and dimensions. Sheets live in LayoutEditor__DrawingsData.__Sheets in project.json; snapshots and projected linework are R2 assets. Every value here is a built-in default; LayoutEditor__Config in Na__AppConfig__Main.json carries the web read-only guard. Paper distances are millimetres.

LayoutEditor__Sheet__Config.LayoutEditor__Sheet__Description: Paper. Sizes are listed landscape (long edge first); portrait swaps them. MarginMm is the border inset; the title block band sits inside the margin at the foot of the sheet, with BlockGapMm of clear paper between it and the drawing area above. ScreenPixelsPerMm is the base on-screen size at zoom 1; printed output is driven by the PDF exporter, never by this value.
LayoutEditor__Sheet__Config.LayoutEditor__Sheet__MarginMmNote: 5 mm, matching a Lantern Designer drawing. A sheet from either app trims to the same border, so the two sit together in one pack rather than reading as output from two different offices.
LayoutEditor__Sheet__Config.LayoutEditor__Sheet__BlockGapMmNote: Clear paper between the drawing area and the title block strip. Without it the strip reads as a row of the drawing rather than as the sheet own footer. Screen sheet and PDF both honour this value.
LayoutEditor__Sheet__Config.LayoutEditor__Sheet__DefaultNameFormatNo: What a new sheet is called until it is named. It carried its place in the pack ('Drawing {index}', and {index} still answers) until the tabs took the Drawing Register's short code: 'D11 - Drawing 5' is two numbers on one tab that need not agree. The number on a tab is the register's alone now, so the default name has none.

LayoutEditor__Style__Config.LayoutEditor__Style__Description: How everything printed on a sheet that is not a view is painted. Read by the chrome module, which draws the on-screen sheet and the PDF from one primitive list. FontFamily is Open Sans, the app face; the PDF exporter embeds the same three TTF cuts so paper matches the screen.
LayoutEditor__Style__Config.LayoutEditor__Style__FrameLabelMinFontMm: A viewport caption sits INSIDE its frame's bottom-left corner, so it cannot grow past the frame the way a caption hung beneath one could. In a frame too narrow for it - a tall thin elevation, a cropped detail - the type sets smaller down to this size rather than truncating, because a scale chopped to '1:12...' is worse than none: it still reads as a number. Only a caption that will not fit at this size is truncated.
LayoutEditor__Style__Config.LayoutEditor__Style__TitleValueWeightNot: Regular, not bold. The PDF embeds Open Sans Light, Regular and SemiBold (the three cuts the app loads), so a title value could print as SemiBold; it stays Regular so the strip still reads as a caption over a value rather than as two bold lines.
LayoutEditor__Style__Config.LayoutEditor__Style__TrackingNote: Letter spacing in millimetres, not ems, because a PDF content stream sets character spacing in the page unit. Both painters add it after every glyph and the text measurer counts it, so a tracked run truncates in the same place on screen as on paper.

LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Description: Two styles (D26). Modern is a vector strip: the Vale logo and one row of fields from Rows, sized and typeset to match a Lantern Designer drawing so the two apps issue the same title block. Classic is the office's scanned title block stretched to the full sheet with the text fields overlaid at the anchors below; A4, A2 and A1 fall back to the A3 scan until their scans are added. Fields default from the project and are editable per sheet.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__HeightMmNote: LANTERN DESIGNER'S STRIP: 10 mm, the height the two apps share, so a drawing from either sits in one pack. THE QR CODE IS AS TALL AS THIS ALLOWS - the strip's height less the symbol's quiet zone - so this is also what decides whether a phone can read a printed drawing: 10 mm prints the project's 29 module symbol at 0.303 mm a module in an 8.79 mm square, which is Lantern Designer's own 8.8 mm code with a larger module than Lantern's 0.267. DO NOT LOWER IT: the console says so whenever the module falls under the floor set in Na__ProjectQr__Config__.json. History: 16 mm once, with each value pinned to the foot of the strip, which read as an empty box with writing in its corners; 10 to match Lantern Designer; 20 for one day (19-Sep-2026) while the code carried the project's full 135 byte address and needed the height, which Adam judged 'too tall, too portrait-feeling, and stretched'; and 10 again on 20-Sep-2026, when the code was given a 42 byte address instead (ProjectQr__Link__LengthNote in that file). Raising it is safe for the code, which simply grows with it - but placed viewports are never moved, so a taller strip can run over drawings already laid out against this one.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__LogoCellWidthM: Was 34 with 1.4 mm of LogoPaddingHMm, which left the mark 1.4 mm from the frame on one side and from the Client cell's rule on the other - Adam, 19-Sep-2026: 'Give me a little space left and right of the logo as well, so it's not so hemmed in.' The mark itself is unchanged: LogoMaxHeightMm and the strip height are what size it (31.1 x 7.6 mm), so widening the cell to 40 and the padding to 4 only adds air, about 4.4 mm either side.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__LogoAspectWidt: The asset is 2048 x 500 px, so 4.096 (re-measured 10-Sep-2026 when the Vale mark was replaced with the Noble Architecture one; the Vale asset was 2000 x 444 and 4.5). The asset cache hands the chrome a data URL and no dimensions, and both painters stretch an image to whatever rectangle they are given, so the aspect has to be stated here rather than measured. It was assumed to be 4.2, which printed the Vale mark 7 percent too tall on every sheet. Re-measure this if the logo file is ever replaced.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__FieldPaddingNo: The label hangs from the top of the strip at FieldLabelOffsetTopMm; the value is optically centred in the band left between FieldPaddingTopMm and FieldPaddingBottomMm. That is what makes a cell read as a small caption over a value, rather than as two runs pinned to opposite edges of a box - which is what pinning the value to the foot of the strip used to give.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__DocumentIdNote: The strip used to call this cell Drawing No. and print whatever sat in Sheet__Fields__DrawingNumber. That field now holds the sequential number alone (D01), so the cell reads the composed DocumentId instead and is labelled for what it actually is: an identifier with the job, the phase and the drawing in it, not a number. The identifier's length barely moves - the job code and the phase are fixed, and the drawing number gains one digit past D99 - so the cell is 24 mm: WW88_T04_D100, the widest code the schema can compose, measures 20.4. See TrueVision__NOTES__DrawingNumberingSchema__.md.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__RowsNote: WidthMm IS PAPER MILLIMETRES, the same on every paper size, the way the logo already is. Until 19-Sep-2026 these were relative shares of the strip, so every cell grew with the paper: on A2 the Client cell was 76 mm for 'Mr P. Samra' and the Document ID 71 mm for twelve characters, while the Drawing Title - the one value that is ever long - was cut off at 92 mm. Adam: 'there are certain fields that are never going to need more size, so they kind of seem needlessly oversized... The one thing that does need the space is the drawing name.' A row with Flex takes what the paper has left over, shared by weight if more than one has it, and its WidthMm is the least it is ever given; the Drawing Title is the one that ships with it. NO VALUE IS CUT OFF WHILE ANOTHER CELL HAS ROOM TO SPARE: a cell whose text will not fit grows, out of the paper's spare room first and then out of the room other cells are not using, which is how Site Address and the title 'grow if absolutely required'. A pack whose values fit therefore has its dividers in the same place on every sheet. On paper too narrow for the strip (A4) the cells give up their unused room before anything is cut. The arithmetic is Na__LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Cells__.js. Widths are measured against Open Sans at FontSizeValueMm, padding included: Client 36 holds 'Mr & Mrs Featherstonehaugh' (33.0); Site Address 70 holds '255 Musters Road, West Bridgford, Nottinghamshire, NG2 7DD' (67.0); Rev, Scale, Date and Drawn By are one 28 mm module - Adam: 'Revision, scale, date, and drawn by can all be the same size' - set by the widest thing any of them says, the site plan's '1:500 & 1:1250 @ ISO A1' (27.9); Status 30 holds the longest entry in Statuses, 'FOR BUILDING CONTROL' (28.6). On A3 landscape that leaves the title 98 mm, enough for PS01's 84 character titles (92.5). A config with no Flex row at all shares the spare room in proportion to WidthMm, which is exactly the old behaviour.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__StatusesNote: What a drawing is issued for: the last cell of the strip, chosen from the Status box in the Sheet panel or on the drawing's row in the Drawing Register. Held per sheet (Sheet__Fields__Status), because a pack is rarely all one thing - one sheet is superseded while the rest go to tender. Listed in the order a job moves through them, which is the order both boxes offer. Add, remove or reword entries here and both boxes follow; a sheet carrying a status that has since left this list keeps it and still shows it. The Status cell is 30 mm, so an entry wider than 'FOR BUILDING CONTROL' borrows room from the Drawing Title - 'FOR BUILDING REGULATIONS' measures 33.1.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__StatusDefaultN: What a sheet prints until a status is chosen for it. Empty on purpose: the cell is drawn with its label and no value. Every drawing made before the field existed would otherwise start claiming a status nobody gave it, and a wrong status on an issued drawing is worse than none. Set it to an entry from Statuses to give new and untouched sheets that one instead.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__QrCellNote: THE RIGHT-HAND END OF THE STRIP IS THE PROJECT'S QR CODE AND A NOTE SAYING WHAT SCANNING IT DOES, so anybody holding a drawing can point a phone at it and be standing in the 3D model. It mirrors the logo cell at the left: an absolute width in paper millimetres off the end of the strip, the same on every paper, with the Rows solved across what is left between the two - so Status is the last FIELD and this cell stands beyond it, in the sheet's bottom right corner. It is modelled on Lantern Designer's terms cell, and at this strip height it is that cell's size: an 8.79 mm code with 0.61 mm round it. These keys say WHERE the code goes and how its note is set. WHAT it says - the address, the words, the symbol's colours, quiet zone and smallest readable module - belongs to the Project QR Code system: 02__Src__AppModules/53__System__ProjectQrCode/Na__ProjectQr__Config__.json. The code needs no size here: it is the strip's HeightMm less the quiet zone it is owed, so it follows the strip. With no project on the address bar, or with that system switched off, there is no cell and the fields keep the whole strip.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__QrCellWidthMmN: The whole cell: the note's column, then the code with its clear margin either side. The code and its margins take 10 mm of this, PaddingHMm and TextGapMm another 2.4, which leaves the note a column of 43.6 mm. MEASURED, NOT GUESSED: every width from 42 to 58 was wrapped against the shipped words in Open Sans at three body sizes, and this column is the one that sets the body at 1.5 mm in TWO LINES OF ALMOST EXACTLY EQUAL LENGTH - '...and view the building' over 'in full 3D, and to freely navigate and take a tour.' - flush without any letter spacing to speak of (0.004 mm). A millimetre either side wraps the same words into one long line and one short, or three with a widow, so re-measure if the words or BodyFontMm change. Lantern Designer's terms cell is 57. Never drawn narrower than the code and its margins, and never wider than a third of the strip, which is the logo cell's own cap.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__QrCellTextGapM: The note stops this far short of the code's quiet zone. The zone alone is 0.61 mm, and a line of type ending that close to the symbol reads as touching it.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__QrCellNoteMinF: ON NARROW PAPER THE NOTE GOES BEFORE ANY FIELD IS CUT. If the whole cell would leave the fields less strip than this, the cell is drawn COMPACT instead: the code at its full size with Note CompactText turned up its left side, 12.4 mm wide in place of 56. Measured in Open Sans on 19-Sep-2026, a sheet's fields need from 193 mm at their text (PS01 with a short title) to 299 mm (a long client, three scales and an 84 character title). So 250 keeps the note on A3 landscape and everything larger - the fields are left 314 mm, which holds the worst of those whole - and drops it on A4 landscape and A3 portrait, where the whole cell would leave 191 mm and the compact one leaves 235; and on A4 portrait. The test is the paper's width and nothing on the sheet, on purpose: every sheet of one size in a pack is then drawn the same way, whatever its title runs to. 0 never goes compact.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__QrCellCompactN: The compact caption is bold, takes the labels' uppercasing and tracking, and reads upward, its baseline on the edge of the code's quiet zone and its capitals standing clear of it to the left. CompactPaddingMm is the clear paper between those capitals and the cell's rule. It has only the code's own 8.79 mm to run along: a caption that will not fit at CompactFontMm is set smaller rather than cut, because half an instruction is no instruction, and one that would have to go under CompactMinFontMm is left out altogether with the band it would have stood in - a code with no caption is still a code, and print too small to read is not a caption. The shipped '3D MODEL' fits at the full 1.6.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__QrCellPaddingN: PaddingHMm is the fields' own FieldPaddingHMm, so the note starts where a field's label would. PaddingVMm is Lantern Designer's: the most the note's block may fill of the strip's height before it loses a line.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__QrCellFontNote: Lantern Designer's heading size, bold, with the labels' uppercasing and tracking, so the cell reads as part of the title block rather than as a sticker on it. The body is regular and muted, and 1.5 where Lantern's is 1.3: it is a lowercase sentence that a client has to be able to read, and two lines of it leave the strip room to spare. It inverts the caption-over-value rhythm of the field cells on purpose - those caption a value the reader is looking for, this one tells them to do something, so the instruction leads.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__QrCellBodyMaxL: The most body lines ever set; fewer when the strip is too low for them (at 10 mm, three fit under the heading). Copy that will not fit ends in an ellipsis rather than overflowing the strip, which on a title block would read as a printing fault. The heading and body are centred in the strip's height as one block, measured from the top of the heading's capitals to the last baseline, so it sits level with the code beside it.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__QrCellJustifyN: Every body line but the last is stretched to the column by letter spacing, so the note reads as a block with a flush right edge beside a square code (Lantern Designer's terms cell does the same). ALL OF THEM OR NONE: if any line would need more than JustifyMaxTrackingMm after every character, the whole block is left at its natural spacing - one flush line over one ragged one reads as a fault, where a wholly ragged block reads as a choice.
LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Config.LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__ClassicFieldAn: Paper-mm anchors per paper size, measured from the top-left of the sheet, for the text overlaid on the scan. FontMm is the value size. Adjust once against the scan and every sheet follows.

LayoutEditor__Scales__Config.LayoutEditor__Scales__Description: Locked scales for 2D viewports (D27). A viewport quotes one of these; the three-way toggle on the Viewport Settings panel steps through them. A site plan viewport quotes one of SitePlanScaleDenominators instead (1:500 block plan, 1:1250 location plan).
LayoutEditor__Scales__Config.LayoutEditor__Scales__SheetLabelNote: What the title block's Scale cell reads. A scale is only true at the paper it was drawn for, so the cell names both: '1:50 @ ISO A2'. Where the viewports on a sheet disagree it lists every scale on it, finest first, joined by ScaleSeparator - '1:50 & 1:100 @ ISO A2' - which tells a reader to check the caption under each viewport, where the old 'As shown' only told them the sheet was mixed. Beyond MaxScales the list is longer than the cell and MixedLabel is quoted instead.
LayoutEditor__Scales__Config.LayoutEditor__Scales__SheetLabelPaperPre: Prefixed to the paper size's Label, so A2 prints as 'ISO A2'. A Label that already opens with the prefix is left alone, so naming a size 'ISO A2' in Sheet PaperSizes never doubles it up. Set to an empty string for a bare 'A2'.

LayoutEditor__Viewport__Config.LayoutEditor__Viewport__Description: Viewports are free rectangles in paper millimetres (D29). A 2D viewport is a window onto a drawing at its scale: edge handles crop or extend the window, dragging inside pans it, corners do nothing. A 3D viewport is a raster snapshot: corners scale it proportionally, edges crop. Snapshot densities are pixels per paper millimetre on screen; the PDF exporter has its own.
LayoutEditor__Viewport__Config.LayoutEditor__Viewport__DefaultStylesNot: What a new viewport starts with. Projected Linework is off so laying out a sheet never triggers a projection; switch it on per viewport when the layout is settled, the way a raster viewport becomes a vector one in SketchUp LayOut. The raster underlay renders either way.
LayoutEditor__Viewport__Config.LayoutEditor__Viewport__ImageZoomNote: 3D viewport zoom (Viewport__ImageZoom): how large the picture is drawn in its frame, as a multiple of its size before zooming. Double-click a 3D viewport and scroll over it to zoom about the cursor, Shift+scroll for fine steps (ImageZoomFineFactor of a notch), Enter to finish; or type a percentage in the Viewport panel. A run of notches is one undo step, announced once the wheel has rested for ImageZoomCommitMs. The frame renders as a window onto the zoomed picture at the frame's own resolution, so a zoom in stays sharp and a zoom out shows more of the scene.

LayoutEditor__Raster__Config.LayoutEditor__Raster__Description: Resolution of the viewport pictures (the 2D underlay and the 3D snapshot) in pixels per paper millimetre, with a longest-side cap per level. Low is 152 dpi, Medium 305 dpi (print quality at paper size) and High 508 dpi, so a picture stays sharp zoomed in. The working level is global, remembered per browser and starts at DefaultLevel; the PDF and the Dev bakes always use ExportLevel. ScaleWithDevicePixelRatio multiplies the working levels by the screen density (up to 2x) so a high-density screen stays sharp.
LayoutEditor__Raster__Config.LayoutEditor__Raster__AntiAliasNote: AntiAliasSamples renders each tile that many times with sub-pixel jitter and averages the results, so a shallow eaves or glazing bar reads as a gradient instead of a staircase. Resolution alone cannot do this: a bigger picture has smaller steps, not fewer. Only 1 (off), 2, 4, 8 and 16 exist; anything else rounds down. The cost is linear - 16 samples is 16 renders - so Low stays at 1 for fast drafting and High carries 16 because it is also the level the PDF and the Dev bakes always use.

LayoutEditor__ViewportCache__Config.LayoutEditor__ViewportCache__Description: Sheets stay rendered while another sheet is shown. Leaving a drawing tab lifts that sheet's viewport frames off the paper whole - the base images, the painted linework, the 3D snapshots and the keys they were rendered under - and coming back puts them straight on again, so flipping between tabs renders nothing. A viewport only renders again when its own key has changed: a resized or re-cropped frame, a pan, a scale, a style or composite weight, its model layers, the raster level, the scene or the model. MaxParkedSheets is how many sheets are kept this way, the least recently shown dropped first; each holds its pictures in memory (a few megabytes a viewport), so lower it on a machine short of memory. 0 switches the cache off. SCREEN ONLY: the PDF never reads this cache - every raster in a PDF is rendered afresh at the Raster block's ExportLevel.

LayoutEditor__Text__Config.LayoutEditor__Text__Description: Sheet text (D31). Sizes are paper millimetres. Weights are the Open Sans cuts the app loads. MULTI-LINE: Shift+Enter starts a new line in the inline editor; Enter commits. LineSpacing is line height as a multiple of the text size; a blank line typed between two others is kept. ROTATION: a selected text item shows a round grip on a short stem off the top of its outline; drag it to turn the text about the middle of its box, or type an angle in the Text panel's Rotation box (degrees clockwise). Shift holds a drag to RotateStepDeg steps; without Shift a drag settles on a right angle once within RotateDetentDeg of one. RotateGripOffsetPx is how far off the outline the grip stands on screen, at any zoom. Right-click a turned item for Reset rotation. The record key is Annotation__RotationDeg, written only while the text is turned, so level text saves exactly as before.

LayoutEditor__Dimensions__Config.LayoutEditor__Dimensions__Description: Sheet dimensions (D32) drawn in paper millimetres. A dimension placed over a 2D viewport reports paper length times the viewport's scale denominator, so it measures the model. MEASURE AT SCALE (DefaultAtScale, the first control of the Dimensions panel, on by default): off every viewport a dimension reports the paper length times the sheet's scale - the scale its 2D viewports share, the biggest drawing's when they differ, the Scales default when it has none - so vectors drawn at scale measure true; switched off, a dimension reports paper millimetres wherever it is. Lengths typed into the Measurements box while one is placed are real sizes at the scale it will read. The record keeps the switch as Dimension__AtScale (true or false); a record from before it has no key and reports what it always did: the model on a viewport, the paper elsewhere. Precision is decimal places; the units suffix follows the figure. ORTHO: hold Shift while the line is being placed (after the second click) and the dimension runs horizontal or vertical whatever its two points are - drag the line above or below them for the x distance between them, beside them for the y. Release Shift and it is aligned again. The record keeps this as Dimension__Orientation ('aligned', 'horizontal' or 'vertical'; a record from before it is aligned). The offset is measured from the start point, and an ortho line stays where it was put while a grip re-picks either point. SIZE MM (TickLengthMm, MinTickLengthMm, MaxTickLengthMm): how large the ticks, arrows or dots at each end are, in paper millimetres. The Dimensions panel's Size mm row, under Ends, sets it per dimension; the record keeps it as Dimension__TickLengthMm. A record from before it has no key and draws at TickLengthMm. TEXT LEADER: click and drag the value off the line and a circular arc runs from the edge of the text back to the centre of the dimension line, tangent to the line there. Dimension__TextDXMm and Dimension__TextDYMm store the paper offset from where the value would have sat; dragging it back within TextLeaderMinMm snaps it home and both keys go. TextLeaderGapMm is the clear paper between the text box and the start of the arc. A record from before it has no keys and the value sits on the line as it always did.
LayoutEditor__Dimensions__Config.LayoutEditor__Dimensions__ExtensionNote: DefaultExtensionMm is how far a new dimension's extension lines run back from the dimension line towards the points it measures, in paper millimetres; null draws the full lines. The Dimensions panel's Ext. lines row sets a start and an end length for each dimension, linked by the padlock between them, and the eyedropper copies them. The points themselves never move: a dimension still measures from them and they are still snap points.
LayoutEditor__Dimensions__Config.LayoutEditor__Dimensions__TextLeaderNote: TextLeaderMinMm is how far, in paper millimetres, a dragged value has to sit from its un-dragged place before the arc is drawn and before a drag keeps rather than snapping home. TextLeaderGapMm is the clear paper between the justified side of the value and the start of that arc. The arc is a circle from the middle of that side to the centre of the dimension line, bulging away from the line so the hook bends outwards. Dragged to the right of the centre the value is left-justified and the arc meets its left; dragged to the left, right-justified, the arc on the right.

LayoutEditor__Panels__Config.LayoutEditor__Panels__Description: The two side columns (Layers on the left; Viewport, Text, Dimensions and Styles on the right). Widths are seeded from here on first use and then remembered for the session.
LayoutEditor__Panels__Config.LayoutEditor__Panels__FocusNote: AccordionSections are the markup sections that behave as one group. FocusSectionOnSelect: selecting something on the sheet, or picking a style with the eyedropper, opens that kind's section and folds the rest of the group, so what is on show is always what is being edited. Several can still be opened by hand to compare them; the next selection tidies them away again. CollapseOthersOnOpen goes further and folds the others the moment one is opened by hand.

LayoutEditor__Navigation__Config.LayoutEditor__Navigation__Description: Wheel zooms about the cursor; middle or right drag pans; touch pinches. Left click is for editing.

LayoutEditor__WebViewer__Config.LayoutEditor__WebViewer__Description: The read-only document viewer the live web build shows in place of the editor. Where authoring is off - anywhere but localhost or an explicitly unlocked device - the drawing tabs, panel columns, toolbar and measurements box are never built, and the drawings and the project specification are shown as one cycled list of documents with a bar at the top and a dock at the bottom. Enabled false hands the web build back the read-only editor it had before this existed. ShowSpecification false leaves the specification out of the list entirely. SwipeMinPx is how far a finger has to travel PAST the edge of the paper before the document changes, so panning a zoomed drawing never turns the page by accident. DoubleTapZoomFactor is how much closer a double tap on a fitted sheet brings it; a double tap on an already magnified sheet fits it again.

LayoutEditor__Snapping__Config.LayoutEditor__Snapping__Description: Object snaps for placing and dragging dimensions and vectors. Two sources: the projected linework inside 2D viewports, and - with SheetObjects on - the sheet's own vectors and dimensions, so a new line can start on the corner of the last one and a polygon can close exactly on its first point. A dragged vector snaps too: the grab point and every vertex are offered, and the nearest snap moves the whole shape. RadiusPx is the pick radius on screen at any zoom. Endpoints and midpoints are candidates; an endpoint wins a near tie, and the sheet's own markup wins a tie with the linework because it sits on top. The item being dragged never offers its own moving point. HiddenLines adds the hidden class as a source. The toggle (toolbar button or the Snap__Toggle key binding) is remembered per browser. MARKER COLOURS say which tool is snapping: blue for vertices (the Draw and Rectangle tools, vertex grips, and a vector being moved), orange for dimensions (the Dimension tool, its grips and its line inference), purple for viewports (carrying one by a point - the ring, the tracking crosses and the frame outline go purple too). The colours live in Na__LayoutEditor__Styles__Main__.css.
LayoutEditor__Snapping__Config.LayoutEditor__Snapping__ViewportCarryNot: Viewports move by a point, the way a block moves in CAD. With the Select tool, hover a 2D viewport's linework: the snap marker shows the point a press would carry it by. Drag, and that point snaps to every OTHER viewport's endpoints and midpoints (and the sheet's own vectors and dimension points). Rest the cursor on another drawing's point for AcquireDwellMs - before the drag or during it - and it is acquired as a tracking point (a small cross): the move then locks level with it or plumb below it, with a dashed guide, which is how two elevations line up side by side without being laid over each other. AcquireMax is how many are held at once, oldest dropped first; they are used up by the move they were acquired for, and Escape clears them. Shift holds the move to the nearer axis. ViewportCarry off makes every press move a viewport the plain way; ViewportTracking off keeps the point snap and drops the tracking. Needs Projected Linework on for the viewport being carried, since the points come from it. The snapping toggle switches all of it off.

LayoutEditor__Clipboard__Config.LayoutEditor__Clipboard__Description: Copy, paste and duplicate for viewports, vectors, text, groups, and a multi-selection of vectors or text (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+D, and the right-click menu). A paste is a new item with a fresh id: a viewport also gets a new name ('{name} copy', then '{name} copy 2' - wording in the Labels block) and every other setting of the one copied; a vector keeps its vertices, closed, edges, fill, gradient and opacities, offset by PasteOffsetMm. Text, groups and a multi-selection paste the same way, with group members remapped to the new ids. A viewport arrives unlocked. On the sheet it was copied from it steps PasteOffsetMm down and right of the original, and again past any copy already there; on another sheet it lands in the same place; from the menu on bare paper its top-left corner goes at the click. Pointing a viewport copy at a different scene clears the copy name so the caption follows the new scene. CopySnapshot lets a 3D copy show the original's stored picture straight away instead of rendering it again. One paste is one undo step. The clipboard is this tab's memory: it survives changing sheet, not a reload.

LayoutEditor__ModelSource__Config.LayoutEditor__ModelSource__Description: Which design phase a viewport draws - the Model Source row of the Viewport panel, and the Model items on a viewport's right-click menu. The choices are the project's modelGroups (the existing building, a scheme, the next scheme); a viewport that names none draws the Project Default, which is the phase the 3D view opens with: the newest group whose label does not say 'existing'. Everything else stays the viewport's own - scene, cut, window, scale, render composites, model layers, edge styles - so a copy of a viewport switched to another phase is the same view of that model: an existing and a proposed elevation that line up exactly. A phase the 3D view does not hold is loaded off-scene the first time a viewport asks for it (the frame says so while it loads), with the same loader and materials as the 3D view, and goes into the scene only for the length of that viewport's render; the 3D view and the Design Phase menu are never touched. MaxCachedPhases is how many such phases stay loaded at once besides the one in the 3D view; beyond it the least recently drawn is let go and loads again when next wanted. The record key is Viewport__ModelSourceId, holding the group's groupId (its folder name), or null for the Project Default.

LayoutEditor__PlanDoors__Config.LayoutEditor__PlanDoors__Description: Doors on 2D viewports: open on plans, shut on elevations and sections. With OpenOnPlans on, a plan draws every door OPEN - in its linework, its base image and the PDF - whatever the 3D view shows, and the model's doors are put straight back afterwards. Each door opens exactly as a click in the 3D view opens it (the ADR / MOD / ROT naming contract): hinged leaves swing, bifolds fold, sliders slide. DrawSwings adds the arc each open hinged leaf's far edge sweeps, at the leaf's floor level and in the Doors layer's line style, one segment per SwingStepDegrees of swing; bifolds and sliders have no arc. With ClickToToggle on, a click on a door in the SELECTED plan viewport closes it and another click opens it again; a press that moves still moves the viewport, and each click waits ClickDelayMs so the two clicks of a double click (entering the content) leave the door alone. The right-click menu offers Close door or Open door for the door under the click, and Open all doors, whatever ClickToToggle says. A lock holds a viewport's frame, not what it draws, so the doors of a locked plan still close and open. Each change is one undo step. The record key is Viewport__ClosedDoors: the door keys drawn shut - an ADR name, or ADR::MOD for one leaf of an exterior double door, whose leaves open one at a time. With ShutOnElevations on, an elevation or section draws every door SHUT - in its linework, its base image and the PDF - whatever the 3D view shows, and has no door to click; off, it draws the doors as the model holds them. 3D viewports always draw the doors as the model holds them.

LayoutEditor__History__Config.LayoutEditor__History__Description: Undo and redo per sheet. Every announced change is one step (a drag is one step); MaxSteps is how many are kept.

LayoutEditor__Selection__Config.LayoutEditor__Selection__Description: How a press finds things on the paper. HitToleranceMm is paper millimetres at 100 percent (it shrinks as you zoom in); a drag starts past DragThresholdMm; grips are drawn GripSizePx square on screen at any zoom, and a picked one GripSizePickedPx so the points the next drag will carry read at a glance. A drag that starts where there is nothing to move - bare paper, the grey stage, a locked viewport - draws a selection box once it has travelled BoxStartPx on screen: dragged to the right a window (blue, solid edge) that takes only what it wholly encloses, dragged to the left a crossing (green, dashed edge) that takes anything it touches as well. BoxBorderPx is the box's edge weight on screen. BoxPreview outlines what the box would take while it is dragged, BoxPreviewPadMm clear of each item. The colours are in Na__LayoutEditor__Styles__Main__.css and the modifiers in Na__LayoutEditor__KeyMappings__.json.
LayoutEditor__Selection__Config.LayoutEditor__Selection__PickDragNote: A press that PICKS is a pick first. The press that selects something, and the second press of a double click (one landing within DoubleClickSlopPx on screen and DoubleClickMs of the last, on the same item), has to travel PickDragPx on screen before it moves anything - so a pick with a wobble in it never nudges a note, and a fast double click always steps inside rather than shifting what it landed on. It applies where a double click means something: a whole-object move, a viewport's frame or content, a leader, a dimension's value. A press on something already selected moves at the ordinary DragThresholdMm, and vertices, measured points, crop handles and the rotate grip always do. DoubleClickMs should not be shorter than the operating system's own double click time (500 ms on Windows). PickDragPx 0 turns the longer travel off.
LayoutEditor__Selection__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__MeasureOffsetAgain: Type another distance to slide it again.
LayoutEditor__Selection__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__MeasureNoOffsetSid: Drag the line to one side, then press Enter.
LayoutEditor__Selection__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__MeasureDimOffsetTi: Drag the line clear of the drawing, then type how far off it should sit and press Enter. Type another distance to slide it again.

LayoutEditor__EditScope__Config.LayoutEditor__EditScope__Description: Editing inside a container, the way SketchUp works. Double-click (or press Enter on) a group to step inside it, and a vector to step inside that: while a container is open, only what is inside it answers a press, everything else on the sheet fades to FadeOpacity, and a vector's points are shown and can be dragged, boxed and added to. Click anywhere outside to step back out one level; Escape closes every container, drops the selection and puts the tools down. MoveToolRequired is the other half of the same idea: with it on, a whole object is only moved by the Move tool (M), so a stray drag with Select cannot shift a viewport or a note - grips, crop handles and the points of an open vector are still dragged by Select, because they edit an object rather than relocate it. Turn it off to have Select drag things about as it did before. GrabRadiusPx is how near a point of the open container a press has to land to be taken as a grab at it rather than the start of a selection box - screen pixels, so it is exactly as forgiving as the grip looks at any zoom. GripToleranceFactor widens the reach of a grip inside its own container, where nothing else is competing for the press: missing a corner by a pixel and dragging the whole object instead is what made dimensions feel untouchable.
LayoutEditor__EditScope__Config.LayoutEditor__EditScope__AutoMoveNote: AutoMoveOnSelect is what stops MoveToolRequired being a chore. Selecting a note, a vector, a leader's bubble or a group is nearly always the first half of moving it, so a Select press on one of the AutoMoveKinds picks the Move tool up by itself and the same press can carry on into the drag. Kinds: annotation (text), shape (vectors), leader (its bubble, note or curve - never its endpoint, which re-points it and stays a grip), group (ordinary and parametric alike), and - left out on purpose - dimension and viewport, which still wait for M so a drawing or a measurement is never shifted by a stray drag. A Move that came up by itself goes back to Select by itself: on a press on anything not listed, when the selection empties, and when a double click steps inside a group, a vector or a text. Press M, or the Move button, for a Move that stays. Several selected items pick Move up only when every one of them is a listed kind. Turn AutoMoveOnSelect off to go back to pressing M every time.

LayoutEditor__Lineweights__Config.LayoutEditor__Lineweights__Description: Printed line weights in points (1 pt = 0.3528 mm), the unit a drawing office reads. These are the defaults a new sheet starts with; the Sheet panel edits them per sheet. ViewportPt is the visible projected linework; the hidden, authored and section classes keep their ratios from the Linework block.

LayoutEditor__Shapes__Config.LayoutEditor__Shapes__Description: The Draw tool's vector shapes (lines, polylines, polygons) and the Rectangle tool's rectangles, which are ordinary closed four-point shapes once drawn. Defaults for a new shape; the Vectors panel edits them. CloseRadiusPx is how near the first point a click has to land to close a polygon. DefaultStroked draws the edges; with it off a new shape is its fill alone, so DefaultFilled must be on as well or the shape would have nothing to show. Dashed edges are off by default; the toggle and its millimetre figures live in Na__LayoutEditor__LineStyleTool__Config__.json.
LayoutEditor__Shapes__Config.LayoutEditor__Shapes__OpacityNote: Opacity runs from 0 (clear) to 1 (solid). DefaultFillOpacity is how solid a new shape's fill is - the Vectors panel's Fill opacity slider. Edges are solid unless Transparent edges is ticked; TransparentEdgeOpacity is where the Edge opacity slider starts when it is. A gradient keeps its own alpha. Shapes from before opacity existed are solid.
LayoutEditor__Shapes__Config.LayoutEditor__Shapes__LineStyleNote: Dashed edges - a toggle on the Vectors panel, off by default. On, the Draw and Rectangle tools place dashed, dotted or dash-dot (centre) lines, with the section lengths in paper millimetres and a scale that stretches them. Owned by Na__LayoutEditor__LineStyleTool__. A shape from before the toggle is a solid line.
LayoutEditor__Shapes__Config.LayoutEditor__Shapes__AtScaleNote: Draw at scale - the first control of the Vectors panel, on by default. On, the sizes typed into the Measurements box while the Draw or Rectangle tool is up are real sizes at the drawing's scale: the scale of the 2D viewport under the first point, or the sheet's scale off every viewport (the scale its 2D viewports share, the biggest drawing's when they differ, the Scales default when it has none). 2500 at 1:50 draws 50 mm of paper, and a dimension measuring it at the same scale reads 2500 back. Off, typed sizes are paper millimetres. A setting of the drawing tools, not of a shape: a shape is paper points either way.

LayoutEditor__Leader__Config.LayoutEditor__Leader__Description: Leaders & Annotation Bubbles: the Leader tool (E) and the Leaders panel. A leader marks a point with an endpoint circle and sweeps to its head on a curve that leaves and arrives level - a straight stub, an S-curve, a straight stub - never a straight rule. Two heads: a Note (multi-line text, one line per Enter) and a Specification bubble (a code centred in a circle, the key the drawing notes will later be pulled in by). The head always extends AWAY from the point, so the side of the point it is placed on decides the handing: to the right a note is left-justified, to the left right-justified, and the leader lands on whichever side of a bubble faces the point. The fill sits behind the text and the line, so a leader masks the drawing it is laid over; FillOpacity lets that show through. Every value here is what a new leader starts with; the Leaders panel edits them, or the selected leader. Weights are printed points, sizes and distances paper millimetres, opacities 0 (clear) to 1 (solid). The records live in each sheet's Sheet__Leaders.
LayoutEditor__Leader__Config.LayoutEditor__Leader__BubbleTextRuleNote: What a new bubble's code field starts with: 'increment' adds one to the number of the newest bubble on the sheet (EE07 becomes EE08, prefix and zero padding kept), 'repeat' offers the same code again, 'fixed' always offers DefaultBubbleText. The field opens with the code selected, so typing another replaces it.
LayoutEditor__Leader__Config.LayoutEditor__Leader__TransparentOpacity: Where the line opacity starts when Transparent lines is ticked on the Leaders panel, so the tick shows a change at once. The line, the endpoint and the bubble edge all take it; unticking makes them solid again.
LayoutEditor__Leader__Config.LayoutEditor__Leader__ShapeNote: The curve and the heads. StubMm is the straight run level with each end, capped at StubMaxFraction of the leader's horizontal run so a short leader is not all stub. CurveTension is how far along the run the S-curve's control points reach: 0.5 is an even S, lower is tighter at the ends. TextGapMm is the clear paper between the line's end and a note's text, TextPaddingMm pads a note's fill, and LineSpacing is a note's line height as a multiple of its text size. TextAttach 'first-line' lands the line level with the middle of a note's first line (the CAD default); 'middle' lands it on the middle of the whole note. BubblePaddingMm is the clearance a code keeps inside its bubble before the bubble grows to fit it. MinLengthMm is how far from the point the head has to be before a leader exists.

LayoutEditor__Eyedropper__Config.LayoutEditor__Eyedropper__Description: The eyedropper (hotkey B) matches properties from one object on the sheet onto another. Click the object that already looks right, then click each object that should match it. StayLoadedAfterApply keeps the picked style on the dropper so a run of items costs one click each; with it off the dropper empties after the first apply and must be re-picked. CopyDimensionOffset is off on purpose: a dimension's offset is where its line sits, so copying it would move the target rather than restyle it. Style travels, content and geometry do not, and the layer never travels in any kind. Unlocked viewports match each other (render composites, frame, caption and scale); a locked viewport is not picked up at all, so the dropper reaches markup and other unlocked viewports through the frame. Shift+B is the palette mode: click an object and its style becomes the setting new objects of that kind are created with - the same traits travel, turned into the panel settings. PaletteSwitchesTool then hands over to the drawing tool for that kind (Text, Dimension, or whichever of Draw and Rectangle drew last); FlashMs is how long the item the style came from pulses.
LayoutEditor__Eyedropper__Config.LayoutEditor__Eyedropper__LeaderNote: Leaders match too: text, line, endpoint, bubble and fill travel between leaders, and a vector's fill and edge opacity travel with its other traits. A leader's type (note or bubble) travels to the palette only, so Shift+B on a bubble sets the Leader tool to draw bubbles, but a paint never turns a note into a bubble.
LayoutEditor__Eyedropper__Config.LayoutEditor__Eyedropper__ViewportNote: Unlocked viewports copy render composites, frame, caption and scale onto other unlocked viewports. A locked viewport (its own lock or its layer) is not a source and not a target, and the eyedropper does not resolve it, so a locked drawing is not detected over the markup on it. Scene, drawing, frame geometry, pan, name, layer, lock and doors stay on that viewport. Viewports do not load the palette: new viewports are added from the panel, not drawn with a tool.

LayoutEditor__Enhance__Config.LayoutEditor__Enhance__Description: The Enhance Whitecard viewport style: the image export's levels and high-pass sharpen, applied to a viewport's render. A white point of 205 sends the shaded whitecard faces to paper white while the linework stays dark.

LayoutEditor__AutoSave__Config.LayoutEditor__AutoSave__Description: A browser draft of every change, put back on the next load while unsaved, and a project save of its own DebounceMs after a sheet is created, renamed, reordered or deleted. Localhost only; the web build is read-only. The draft is written DraftDebounceMs after the editing pauses rather than inside every click - it is a synchronous disk write of every sheet, so doing it per change stalled the editor - and it is flushed when the tab is hidden or closed.
LayoutEditor__AutoSave__Config.LayoutEditor__AutoSave__CloseGuardDescri: CloseGuardEnabled asks the browser's own leave-site question before the window, the tab or the PWA closes on work the project has not been told about - sheets not yet saved, or a specification not yet synced. Content edits (viewports, text, dimensions, vectors) deliberately do not auto save, so the editor can hold a whole session behind the Save Sheets button, and Ctrl+W took it with nothing asked. The draft is flushed as the question goes up, so the answer decides when the work is picked up again rather than whether it survives. The wording belongs to the browser: every current one replaced the custom message years ago. Editable sessions only. Turning this off returns the editor to closing without a word.

LayoutEditor__Linework__Config.LayoutEditor__Linework__Description: Paper-millimetre stroke widths for the projected linework inside sheet viewports (they print at these widths at any scale). Colours follow the Projected Linework appearance block so a sheet matches its scene.

LayoutEditor__Pdf__Config.LayoutEditor__Pdf__Description: jsPDF at true paper size. 2D viewports write the projected linework, dimensions and text as vectors; underlays and 3D viewports are placed as raster images at the Raster block's export level. The vendored UMD build is injected as a classic script on first use. Open Sans is fetched as TTF (the same three cuts the app paints with) and embedded in every document, so Download PDF does not fall back to Helvetica.
LayoutEditor__Pdf__Config.LayoutEditor__Pdf__FilenamePatternNote: Tokens: {drawingCode} the sheet's Drawing No. field as the title block prints it (PS01_T02_D01); {drawingName} the sheet's tab name with its leading sheet number stripped and run together in PascalCase (D01 - Floor Plans -> FloorPlans); {paperSize} A4/A3/A2/A1; {revision} the Revision field prefixed Rev (RevA); {date} today, the day the file was issued, as DD-MMM-YYYY. {projectCode} and {sheetName} still answer, so a pattern configured before these existed keeps working. Every token but the date comes from the sheet the way the title block reads it, so the file name and the drawing inside it cannot disagree. Anything outside A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _ and - becomes an underscore.
LayoutEditor__Pdf__Config.LayoutEditor__Pdf__FontFamilyNote: jsPDF family name for the embedded cuts. No space: jsPDF looks fonts up by this exact id. The screen CSS family remains 'Open Sans'.
LayoutEditor__Pdf__Config.LayoutEditor__Pdf__FontsNote: One TTF per jsPDF style. Weight is the Open Sans cut the app already loads (300 Light, 400 Regular, 600 SemiBold). Style is the jsPDF face name setFont asks for: light, normal, bold. Local FontBasePath is tried first (same origin); FontCdnBase is the fallback, matching Na__CoreUi__Styles__Fonts__.css.

LayoutEditor__Specification__Config.LayoutEditor__Specification__Description: The Project Specification tab: every drawing note of the project, in groups. A group has a prefix (GN, SN, EE) and a title; a note has a title and its specification text. A note's code is its group's prefix and its place in the group, zero-padded to NumberDigits - GN01, EE02 - so moving a note up or down, moving it to another group or changing its group's prefix renumbers it. Specification bubbles on the sheets link to a note by its id, not its code, so a renumber reaches every bubble on every sheet. The specification is a file of its own (FileName) beside TrueVision__ProjectData__.json, kept locally in the project folder so an agent can edit it on disk, and written to the same R2 key on Sync. LegacyFileName is the previous R2 name, read only when FileName is not there yet. The file is read when the drawing editor opens. Every edit is kept in this browser at once (DraftEnabled, written DraftDebounceMs after the typing pauses); Sync writes the whole file to R2 and to the local copy, and first asks whether to replace a cloud copy that changed since it was read (ConfirmCloudOverwrite). HistorySteps is the tab's own undo depth.
LayoutEditor__Specification__Config.LayoutEditor__Specification__RevisionNot: The specification is a document that gets issued, so it carries a revision and a number of its own, the way each sheet carries a Rev and a Drawing No. Both are typed in the Project Specification bar, both print on the document, and both name the downloaded file through the shared Pdf FilenamePattern. DefaultRevision is what an untouched specification opens at, and what a specification written before these fields existed is read as. DocumentNumberSuffix is appended to the project code when no number has been typed, so PS01 gives PS01_SPEC; type PS01_T02_SPEC over it to sit with the sheets.
LayoutEditor__Specification__Config.LayoutEditor__Specification__StarterGrou: The groups Add standard groups creates on a project with no specification. IsGeneral marks a group of general notes: they are listed on every sheet's notes margin, after the notes that sheet's bubbles link to.

LayoutEditor__MarginNotes__Config.LayoutEditor__MarginNotes__Description: The notes margin a sheet can carry down its right-hand side, from the top of the border to the title block. Switched on per sheet with the Notes button on the toolbar or in the Margin Notes panel; drag its left edge to make it wider or narrower. It lists the specification notes the sheet's bubbles link to, in specification order, then the general notes. Distances and text sizes are paper millimetres except the divider and rule (printed points). TextSizeMm is the body (2 mm); titles are TitleScale times that. PaddingMm is the left and top/foot inset; PaddingRightMm is the clearance before the sheet's right border, a little more so wrapped lines do not clip. A note reads as its code, CodePipe, then its title, with the body wrapped to the full inner width. A faint RuleColour line at RulePt sits between notes, centred in the gap between them: NoteGapMm is the least that gap can be, and decides what fits; when every note fits and the column has room left at the foot, every gap opens by the same amount, up to NoteGapMaxMm. IncludeGeneralNotes and GroupHeadings are what a newly switched-on margin starts with.

LayoutEditor__Measurements__Config.LayoutEditor__Measurements__Description: The Measurements box at the bottom right of the sheet (Na__LayoutEditor__Measurements__), SketchUp's VCB. While the Draw, Rectangle or Dimension tool is up it reads out what is being drawn as it is drawn - a line's length, a rectangle's width x height, a dimension's span and then its line's offset - and a value typed while drawing is used on Enter, with no click into the box first: Draw places the next point that far along the rubber band (its direction, so snaps, Shift and the arrow key axis lock aim it); Rectangle lands the opposite corner (3000 x 2000 or 3000,2000; one figure is a square; typed straight after a rectangle lands, it resizes that rectangle); Dimension picks the end that far along the band, then puts the line that far from what it measures. Dragging a vertex of a finished vector wakes the box the same way: the reading is the drag's length, and a typed value moves the vertex that far along the inferred direction (the original vertex toward where it is being dragged; a minus sign runs the other way) and finishes the drag so the pointer cannot pull it back. Dragging a viewport's frame (not a handle, not the drawing inside) wakes it too: a typed value moves the frame that far along the drag, at the viewport's scale (or the sheet's for a 3D viewport). A number with no unit is millimetres; add m, cm or mm for another (2.5m), commas may group thousands (2,500) and a minus sign draws the other way. The line above the box shows how a value is being read as it is typed. AT SCALE: with Draw at scale on (Shapes DefaultAtScale) lines, rectangles and a dragged vertex take and show real sizes at the drawing's scale - the 2D viewport under the first point (or the vertex), or the sheet's scale elsewhere - so 2500 at 1:50 is 50 mm of paper; off, they are paper millimetres. A dimension uses Measure at scale (Dimensions DefaultAtScale). The chip at the right of the box shows the scale in use. Precision is the decimal places a reading shows (trailing zeros dropped), UnitsSuffix follows it, PairSeparator joins a rectangle's two sizes, HintMs is how long a message above the box stays, and EdgeGapPx keeps the box clear of the stage's scrollbars. The keys it reads are in Na__LayoutEditor__KeyMappings__.json under MeasurementsBox.

LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__TextSelectedNote: Editing the selected text. Shift+Enter adds a line; Enter finishes. Drag the round grip to rotate it; hold Shift for steps.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__MenuForceRenderShe: Re-render every viewport on this sheet
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__TabLabelFormatNote: What a sheet is called on its tab, the toolbar and every list that names one: {code} is the short code cut from the Drawing Register's number ('PS01_T02_D03' gives 'D03'), {name} the sheet's short name. The whole drawing number stays on the tab's hover and the title block. With {name} empty this is also the fixed text in front of the Sheet panel's Name box ('D03 -').
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__SheetTabEditTitle: Double-click to rename, drag to reorder
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__SheetNamePlacehold: Short tab name, e.g. Floor Plans
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__CommonFieldsTitle: Client and Site Address are the project's, shared by every drawing in the pack - typing either one retypes them all. Untick to give this one sheet its own.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__StatusTitle: What this drawing is issued for. It prints in the last cell of the title block, and can also be chosen on the drawing's row in the Drawing Register. The list is LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Statuses.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__SheetNameCodeTitle: Drawing {number}. The number comes from the Drawing Register and follows it by itself - type only the short name.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__SitePlanNoData: No site plan data for this project. In SketchUp: GLB Builder, Export Site Plan Data, into 30__TrueVision__AppContent/SitePlan__DrawingData.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__SitePlanNoLayers: No site plan layers loaded yet.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__NoSelection: Select a viewport on the sheet.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__NoSheets: No sheets yet. Add one from the Dev menu or the + tab.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ViewerPdfTitle: Download this sheet as a PDF at paper size
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__SavedLocalMessage: Sheets saved to R2 and locally.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__SavedLocalFailedMe: Sheets saved to R2, but the local copy was not written: {error}.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__DeleteSheetPrompt: Delete the sheet "{name}"? Its viewports, text and dimensions go with it.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__SnapToggleTitle: Snap to endpoints and midpoints of the linework and the sheet's own vectors and dimensions (F3)
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__EditingViewNote: Editing viewport content: drag to reposition, Enter or Esc to finish
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__EditingView3dNote: Zoom {zoom}%: scroll to zoom (Shift for fine steps), drag to reposition, Enter to finish
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ZoomTitle: How large the 3D picture is drawn in its frame, as a percentage of its size before zooming. Type any value, to a decimal place. Or double-click the viewport and scroll over it to zoom about the cursor.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ZoomResetTitle: Back to 100%, centred in the frame.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ShowFrameTitle: The border and caption round this viewport, on the sheet and in the PDF. Untick once the sheet is set out, to title the view yourself.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__CaptionNeedsFrame: The caption shows with the frame. Tick Frame to show it.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__DraftRestored: Unsaved sheet changes from this browser were restored. Save Sheets keeps them.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ToolDimensionTitle: Place a dimension in three clicks (D): start, end, then where the line sits. Hold Shift while placing the line for a horizontal or vertical dimension.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ToolRectangleTitle: Draw a rectangle (R): click one corner then the opposite corner, or drag from one to the other. Shift keeps it square, Esc abandons it.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ToolEyedropperTitl: Match properties (B): click the object to copy FROM, then each object to copy ONTO. Alt+click picks a new source, Esc finishes. Shift+B or Shift+click: use an object's style for new objects instead.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__EyedropperPickHint: Eyedropper: click the object to copy properties FROM.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__EyedropperLoadedHi: Holding {source} properties - click each {source} to apply. Alt+click picks a new source, Esc finishes.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__EyedropperLocked: That layer is locked - unlock it first.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__EyedropperLockedVi: That viewport is locked - unlock it first.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__EyedropperPaletteH: Palette: click an object to use its style for new objects of that kind. Esc finishes.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__EyedropperPaletteS: New {kinds} will be drawn like that {kind}. Click another to set another, Esc finishes.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__TextCopied: Copied text. Ctrl+V pastes it, on this sheet or another.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__GroupCopied: Copied group. Ctrl+V pastes it, on this sheet or another.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__SelectionCopied: Copied {count} items. Ctrl+V pastes them, on this sheet or another.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ShapeCopied: Copied vector. Ctrl+V pastes it, on this sheet or another.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__LeaderCopied: Copied leader. Ctrl+V pastes it, on this sheet or another.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__TextPasted: Pasted text in the same place.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__GroupPasted: Pasted group in the same place.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__SelectionPasted: Pasted {count} items in the same place.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ShapePasted: Pasted vector in the same place.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__LeaderPasted: Pasted leader in the same place.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ViewportCopied: Copied "{name}". Ctrl+V pastes it, on this sheet or another.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ShapeSelectedNote: Editing the selected shape. Hold Shift over an edge and click to add a vertex. Dragging snaps to the linework. While dragging a vertex, type a length into the Measurements box to move it that far along the drag.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ShapeDefaultsNote: Nothing selected: these settings apply to new shapes.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ShapeEitherNote: Edges and fill are either or: switching one off switches the other on, so a shape always shows.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ShapeDrawNote: Draw tool (L): click points, click the first point to close a polygon, Enter or double-click to finish a line, Esc to abandon, Ctrl+Z to take the last point off.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ShapeRectangleNote: Rectangle tool (R): click one corner then the opposite corner, or drag from one to the other; Shift keeps it square; Esc, Space or a right click abandons it. Both corners snap like the Draw tool's points. The result is an ordinary closed vector, so the Select tool drags its corner grips like any polygon's and the Vectors panel restyles it.
LayoutEditor__Labels__Config.LayoutEditor__Labels__ShapeAxisNote: Arrow keys lock the axis for the next point (left or right locks across, up or down locks down the page); press the same key again to release. Shift holds the nearer axis for as long as it is down. Either way the axis is kept and a snap only supplies the distance along it, so lock an axis and hover a vertex to line the edge up with that vertex - which is how the last corner of a rectangle is found. The shape closes when the point would LAND on the first one, not when the cursor passes near it.

LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Descripti: Pack numbering and PDF defaults. Revision notes live in the self-contained LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister project block. Sheet ids remain unchanged.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Typograph: Point sizes for the register document. The body size is PdfFontPt; everything else is set against it so the page keeps one hierarchy. Open Sans is embedded, so these are the sizes the reader actually gets.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__SpacingNo: Table rhythm in millimetres. RowPadMm is the space above and below a row's text block, so a one-line row is RowPadMm*2 + LineMm tall and every row is vertically centred. CellPadMm is the gutter inside a column. Raise RowPadMm to open the table up further.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__ColumnsNo: Column order, heading, alignment and sizing. Width is measured from the real embedded font: a fixed column takes the width of its widest cell so codes and scales never wrap mid-token, and the one flex column absorbs the slack. MinMm floors a column at its heading; the flex column's MinMm is the point past which it starts wrapping instead of shrinking.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__TypeColum: TYPE was dropped on 19-Sep-2026 when the three code columns arrived. It printed the constant "Drawing" on every row - the register builds it in code and no sheet can say anything else - and eight columns do not fit A4 portrait: adding it back breaks "Drawing" across two lines and takes ISO A2 and Rev B with it. The row still carries type, so restoring the column here is one line, but the page needs to go landscape first.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__StatusCol: STATUS IS CHOSEN IN THE REGISTER'S EDIT TABLE BUT IS NOT A PRINTED COLUMN. The Edit table has a Status box on every row (the list is LayoutEditor__TitleBlock__Statuses) and the title blocks print it, but the PDF below is A4 portrait with seven columns already in it. Measured 19-Sep-2026 with the real fonts on PS01's four rows at PdfMarginMm 14 (182 mm of text width): with STATUS added the columns ask for 200 mm, so the shortfall rule takes room off every column - STATUS is left 21 mm of text room where 'FOR CONSTRUCTION' needs 31 and breaks onto two lines, and SCALE's '1:500 & 1:1250' breaks with it. The same wall TYPE hit. Every row carries status, so printing it is one line here ({ "Key": "status", "Heading": "STATUS", "Align": "left", "Flex": false, "MinMm": 18 }), but the page needs to go landscape, or lose a column, first.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__ColumnsSc: The first three columns are the document code taken apart: drawingNo is the sequential number the register writes and the tabs read, phase is which stage of the job the drawing belongs to, and documentCode is those two behind the project code, composed. Read left to right they build the identifier the title block prints. See TrueVision__NOTES__DrawingNumberingSchema__.md.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__PhasesNot: The stage of the job a drawing belongs to, and the middle third of every document code. A project carries several at once - a planning set stays live while building regulations drawings are started - so the phase is held per sheet, not per project. Code is what prints; Name is what the register's Phase box offers, in Adam's own words for them - a select is as wide as its widest option, so a long name here sets the width of the whole column. Adding a phase here adds it to that box everywhere.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__DefaultPh: What a sheet is read as when its phase has never been set, including every drawing made before the phase existed. Adam chose T01 on 19-Sep-2026: a drawing that has not declared its stage is a concept drawing, and saying so is honest where guessing Planning would quietly mislabel a whole back catalogue.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__DocumentC: How the three parts become the one identifier the title block prints and the PDF file is named after: {project} the job number from the project data (PS01, EB03, RB05), {phase} the sheet's phase code, {drawing} the register's sequential number. COMPOSED, NEVER STORED - a renumber or a phase change reaches the title block, the register and the file name at once, and cannot leave them disagreeing. A part that is empty takes its separator with it, so a project with no phase set reads PS01_D01 rather than PS01__D01. A sheet may still carry a typed Sheet__Fields__DocumentId, which wins over this for that sheet alone.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Letterhea: The register PDF wears the Project Specification's letterhead - the office mark left, the running head and the issue right, a hairline under - because the two are tabs of one pack and were reading as two different documents. LetterheadLogoAspect must match the logo asset: it is stated, not measured, because jsPDF stretches an image into whatever rectangle it is given. RegisterNumberSuffix makes the document number, PS01_REGISTER, sitting beside the specification's PS01_SPEC.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__CollapseS: A sheet's Scale field is typed as the title block prints it ('1:50 @ ISO A2'), which repeats the SIZE column word for word and was the main reason the table wrapped. True prints the scale alone ('1:50') when its paper suffix matches that row's SIZE. Set false to print the Scale field verbatim. The stored field is never changed either way.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__EmptyCell: Printed in the muted ink wherever a table cell has nothing in it, so a never-numbered sheet or an unrevised drawing reads as a stated blank rather than as a hole. Set to "" to leave such cells truly empty.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__PreviewNo: The Read view rasterises the exact bytes the download sends. The canvas is drawn at the display's own pixel density, up to PreviewMaxPixelRatio, so the preview is not a soft upscale of a 1.25x render. PreviewPageWidthPx is the CSS width a page is laid out at.
LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__Config.LayoutEditor__DrawingRegister__AccentNot: The drawings' own ink colour, used for the header rule and the table's head rule so the register reads as part of the pack it lists.
